output.name: Tirun
output.myth:
They came home keel-up on a grey morning, Tirun, with no crew in her and no oars shipped. The women of the north shore turned her with ropes and found her lamps still burning, though the seal oil should have gone a month before. Tavo the Gale had been out that week, laughing at the boats, and would not say what he had done. Ennu cut her sailcloth open and found only salt and bone. Hesk counted the lamps and came up one short of the crew.

Hatun, the Bailing Gourd, hangs fourteen degrees west, where Tavo once filled a boat with a mother and her children, so he is never far off. Sathun, the Waiting Long-Tail, lies fourteen degrees east, where a fisherman's wife still flies her kite at dusk, watching past the rocks for her man. So the lamps burn for everyone who went past the Leeward edge and did not come back. When you go out, hang a lamp under your own hull. If it still burns when you return, somebody is waiting for you.
output.finding: Find Hatun, the Bailing Gourd, and from it look a fist and a little over eastward along the Leeward band to the lamp that is Tirun, with the Waiting Long-Tail a little beyond it.
